claim.value: Without random assignment, observed differences may reflect roster timing rather than the release.
claim.scope: A possible alternative explanation in a nonrandomized comparison, not an assertion that timing caused a particular difference.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly supplies both the absence of random assignment and roster timing as a possible alternative explanation.

signal_basis.value: The release comparison yields a difference in first-publication rates over the specified follow-up, in a comparison without random assignment.
signal_basis.scope: The nonrandomized case of the described release comparison.

provenance.rationale: P022 identifies the measured difference and follow-up; P035 explicitly identifies the nonrandomized comparison condition.
The claim is supported as a possibility statement; no unresolved empirical relation is required to license it.

rationale: Without random assignment, comparison groups can differ in roster timing, which can affect publication during follow-up. The observed rate difference therefore leaves timing available as an alternative explanation. The claim asserts only this possibility.
uncertainty: Whether roster timing actually explains any particular difference remains undetermined; the claim does not assert that it does.
